sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Al–Bi binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AlBi-06Kim.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L1 → (Al) + L2, lies at 658.6 °C.
The Al–Bi system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as miscibility gap, monotectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of S.S. Kim, T.H. Sanders, Jr., Modelling Simul. Mater. Sci. Eng., 14, 1181-88(2006). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The monotectic reaction L1 → (Al) + L2 is calculated at 658.6 °C, with L1 at x(Bi) = 0.003.
The dataset places a eutectic (L → (Al) + (Bi)) at 271.2 °C; the composition of L is x(Bi) = 0.999.
Table 1 compares the calculated temperatures with experimental values from the literature [3–5]; in this synthetic document those values and references are fictitious.
The upper stability limit of (Bi) is 271.4 °C.
At 1400 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 19170 J/mol, at x(Bi) = 0.440.
For the equiatomic liquid at 1400 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −7.71 kJ/mol-atom.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
